scope: Opt-in TOTP, recovery codes and login gating within P2. Not full P2, installed-Windows, physical-authenticator, P0-P11 or release acceptance.
implemented: Additive migrations 090/091 persist account-bound encrypted TOTP secrets, expiring/supersedable setup state, replay counters, recovery hashes, replacement generation and a shared durable attempt budget.

Password-authenticated setup, current-code confirmation, server-side cancellation and password-plus-factor disabling. Recovery replacement uses a generation compare-and-swap to prevent two stale requests both succeeding.
Six-digit SHA-1 TOTP with 30-second steps and at most one adjacent step; successful enrollment and login verification consume the step atomically.

Ten independently random 128-bit recovery codes are displayed once. Account-separated SHA-256 hashes are stored; one atomic SQL operation consumes a code. Replacing or disabling invalidates old codes.

Login checks MFA only after password/account-state verification and before presence changes, session rows, access tokens or cookie issuance. MFA challenges do not create partial authenticated sessions.
Account-bound management requests reject stale account IDs. Secret-bearing responses use no-store and internal MFA records cannot serialize secrets through JSON.

TR/EN settings enrollment, one-time code presentation/acknowledgement, regeneration, explicit disable confirmation, errors/retry and unsaved-secret navigation guards. Manual authenticator-key entry is provided; QR scanning is not.

Login UI accepts an authenticator or recovery code and focuses the challenge. Changing identity clears the previous factor. A saved desktop password cannot bypass MFA; manual password/factor entry remains required.
Credential login does not auto-refresh/replay its 401 challenge. MFA writes can proactively refresh an expired session but do not retry a one-time-code rejection automatically.

Five security attempts per account per five-minute window are persisted in SQLite. A server restart does not reset the stored budget. Other P2 security-attempt limits still require implementation/acceptance.

User hard deletion explicitly removes MFA state even when remote database foreign keys are not enforced. Key preservation and the prohibition on rollback to an MFA-unaware server are documented in implementation/MFA_OPERATIONS.md.

Browser: acknowledging the recovery codes removed them from the view.

Browser: disabling required password, another unused recovery code and a separate confirmation. A later independent HTTP password-only login succeeded.
